What changes when one of us changes?
Two people can welcome an arrangement today and need something different tomorrow. What happens to the work, the resources, and their willingness to ask again?
Synthetic worked case · fictional participants A and B · no calibrated behavioral predictions

children: When a request returns, it brings a history.

A respectful refusal can leave a concern heard. A promise can create expectations that only later work fulfills. A capacity limit can leave work unfinished without showing unwillingness. This small household makes those distinctions visible over time.
Compare four orientations under the same kinds of change. Adjust values, capacity and the history of responses, then inspect what the assumed rules produce. No orientation wins by definition.
Begin with an arrangement, then introduce change.
A and B are fictional partners. Their labels do not assign sex, authority or moral standing. Keep their stated values, the material outcomes and the possibility of review separate.

Choose whose inputs to edit and when they apply. “After change” applies from period 5; later authored events remain visible. Rates apply throughout the run. These controls express assumptions, not a diagnosis.
How this person handles the other’s requests
Defaults are 0.10 heard, 0.25 dismissed, 0.04 kept, 0.20 missed and 0.00 capacity loss. They are authored choices without empirical calibration.
These are opening resource assumptions. Unfinished domestic work and money carry forward between periods.
Follow the household, one period at a time.
Compare both people on the same fixed scale. Move through time to inspect what each period changed.
The timeline will show each person separately. Closing willingness affects the following period.
Dashed vertical lines mark authored input changes. The solid marker follows your selected period.
Twelve periods; change begins at period 5
Read exact values for all 12 periods
The values appear when the model is ready.
An authored 0–1 index, not a probability or a measure of consent, happiness or trust. Closing values affect the following period.
The interactive example is loading. The notebook remains readable without it.
Inspect this period’s work, responses and resources
Values, achieved work, capacity and willingness will appear here.
Each account remains distinct; a household average cannot stand in for either person.
What happened, and what evidence changed willingness?
Choose a period to inspect its request, agreement and delivery history.
Work delivered, unpaid backlog, paid work, expenses and reserve.
Whose request was heard; which agreement was kept; what remains unknown.
Closing willingness and unfinished work carry into the next period.
Interactive controls require the site’s algebra runtime. The assumptions and all 66 attributed claims are available in the inspection notebook.
An allocation is one question. Correction is another.
What does each person want, and which compromises do they welcome? Distinct values need not prevent practical cooperation.
Can the work and essential expenses be covered? A desirable division on paper can exceed available capacity.
Can either person raise a concern, refuse a proposal or reopen a decision? Being heard is different from getting the requested remedy.

This model does not compute happiness, consent, love, dignity or the moral legitimacy of an arrangement. Its commitment to retaining a route for correction is a declared normative proposal. You can reject it or leave without assessment.
A household is also a relationship.
The Field holds this experiment because choices change what can happen next. These questions place the model beside the rest of the corpus:
what remains owed when an arrangement becomes difficult?
what can be reopened, and who can ask?
who authorizes a choice on someone else’s behalf?
how might a relationship find contact again?
These relationships locate the example; they do not provide empirical validation for its authored rules.
A few things I’ve built. A few things I’m still trying to understand.

children: This is an executable synthetic example with uncalibrated parameters. It calculates consequences of declared assumptions; it does not establish how actual households behave or adjudicate the tweet’s empirical predictions.

Values, reported satisfaction, material feasibility and the practical ability to renegotiate are distinct. No calculated willingness value stands in for consent, happiness or trust. Standing is unchanged by work, refusal, withdrawal or leaving.
Four orientations; four sets of tradeoffs.
A primarily provides income; B primarily manages the home. They value continuity, distinct responsibilities and an inherited account of family life.
Both welcome their roles, the work is feasible, and each contribution is recognized. Exceptions can be understood as care within a continuing commitment.
The partners attach different meanings to the same roles, or an assigned responsibility exceeds the person's capacity while the label conceals that mismatch.
Both pursue paid work and share domestic responsibility. They value reciprocity, participation and equal standing.
They agree what equality means, include planning and coordination as work, and accept practical exceptions.
A task count looks equal while effort, responsibility or rest differs; alternatively, enforcing exact symmetry becomes an unwanted burden for both.
Tasks follow current skill, available time and preference rather than fixed identities. They value practicality and complementary strengths.
The allocation fits present capacities, and either partner can acquire skills or request a different allocation.
The same person repeatedly absorbs work because they are already better at it; the arrangement protects present efficiency while leaving the other without practice or alternatives.
One partner's career, study or caregiving project receives priority for a defined period, with a later change of emphasis. They value shared projects and reciprocity across time.
The initial sacrifice is welcome, resources suffice, and the later opportunity remains meaningful and feasible.
Future reciprocity is vague, the priority period continually extends, or the promised later opportunity disappears.
These arrangements can overlap. Equal standing does not require identical task shares. Specialization does not require unilateral authority. A and B’s sex does not select a role.
Carry a household through twelve periods

At each opening, apply authored changes to values, capacity or demand. Period 5 introduces the selected change. Some experience patterns change again at period 9. Carry allocation, backlog, money and each person’s closing willingness into the next period.
Separate a request from a successful revision

Opening willingness determines whether a request is voiced and bounds review and task movement. A respectful hearing can occur without an acceptable proposal. Dismissive handling blocks the joint proposal. Unknown handling supplies no positive or negative request evidence.
A signed agreement is followed by execution

A passing revision supersedes the previous allocation. Each assignment covers its share of the current domestic task pool, including backlog. Capacity determines achievable work; the authored delivery fraction determines how much of that achievable work is done. Unfinished work remains visible.

delivered domestic work = achievable domestic work × delivery fraction
next backlog = current domestic task pool − total domestic work delivered
next reserve = opening reserve + paid income − covered expenses
For observer willingness w and rate g or l:

positive evidence: w′ = w + g × (1 − w)
negative evidence: w′ = w × (1 − l)
neutral or learning disabled: w′ = w

The requester receives heard or dismissed evidence. Each person receives evidence about the other’s executed commitment. Capacity-only shortfall defaults to neutral; implementation-only shortfall may reduce willingness. Mixed attribution, unknown quality, empty obligations and superseded allocations have no automatic effect.
Keep the feedback delayed and attributable

Record response evidence, explicit outreach and delivery evidence in order. Closing willingness becomes available next period; it cannot change the current review retrospectively. An invitation and a hearing about the same interaction do not manufacture two hearing gains. No request is inferred from silence.
A limit is different from a refusal

Capacity-limited delivery and incomplete implementation are different accounting outcomes. Neither alone diagnoses intention or bad faith. The delivery fraction is an authored input; the model does not infer its cause. Higher income can coexist with an unfulfilled task commitment.
Explicit respectful outreach can support reopening from zero willingness. Changed practice does not erase earlier events, restore the former value automatically or establish forgiveness.
What symmetry does and does not establish

The local rules use participant-neutral labels. Swapping A and B is a useful test of hidden role assumptions. The retained audit found local exchange symmetry but 28 order-sensitive trajectories in the 100-case design. Whole-run exchange invariance is therefore not established: agenda order and ties can affect later history.
This boundary prevents a symmetric-looking interface from claiming a stronger fairness result than the arithmetic supports. No score ranks the worth of either participant.

The primary source is Noah Revoy’s post of 6 November 2026. Direct retrieval failed; the text and its quoted post were retrieved through FxTwitter that day. This is one mediated evidence family, without an immutable source snapshot. Later edits require checking the decomposition again. The quoted image is outside the case.

Claims 1–62 paraphrase Noah Revoy’s assertions. Claims 63–66 paraphrase the quoted IterIntellectus post. These are attributed propositions, not endorsed findings. Classification names the evidence or argument needed; it does not supply that evidence.
Increasing a husband's domestic work worsens his marital relationship.
Increasing a husband's domestic work decreases his wife's happiness.
Increasing a husband's domestic work decreases his earnings.
Increasing a husband's domestic work increases divorce probability.
Increasing a husband's domestic work decreases the couple's sexual frequency.
Increasing a husband's domestic work decreases their eventual number of children.
Increasing a wife's earnings does not improve her marriage.
Modern women have not received adequate preparation for being wives.
Modern women have not received adequate preparation for motherhood.
Modern women dislike hearing this assessment.
Their great-grandmothers would endorse the assessment.
The author's great-grandmother repeatedly expressed the assessment.
Greater competence would let women complete twice the domestic output in half the time.
Insufficient skill causes difficulty performing a task.
Repeated difficulty attributable to insufficient skill produces resentment toward the task.
A husband taking over his wife's domestic work does not improve her competence.
Taking over that work prevents her from developing competence.
Improving competence is the appropriate remedy for the domestic difficulty described.
An inefficient employee should receive help improving skills.
An inefficient employee should receive help improving systems.
An inefficient employee should receive help improving efficiency.
The person responsible for assisting that employee should not abandon their own responsibilities to perform the employee's job.
Taking over the employee's job causes neglect of that person's own work.
Some of that work can be performed only by that person.
Neglecting that work endangers the enterprise.
The business principle transfers appropriately to family organization.
Analogy requiring a bridge · Noah Revoy
A sole-breadwinner husband has a responsibility to earn income.
He has a responsibility to provide for the family.
He has a responsibility to protect the family.
He has a responsibility to lead the family.
Domestic chores divide attention available for his primary work.
That divided attention reduces his capacity to excel at his primary work.
A wife should become competent at managing the home.
A husband should become competent at providing for the home.
Taking over a wife's responsibilities does not make her a better wife.
Asking a wife to take over a husband's responsibilities does not make him a better husband.
Excellence within these respective roles produces a thriving family.
Causal claim dependent on a definition of thriving · Noah Revoy
Wives tell husbands that additional domestic help would make them happier.
Husbands should give those requests less weight.
What a person requests can differ from what benefits that person.
The wife described needs greater competence.
The wife described does not need reduced responsibility.
Husbands should develop the ability to refuse requests.
Wives will sometimes request things their husbands cannot provide.
Children will sometimes request things their mothers cannot provide.
A good husband cannot agree to every request.
A good father cannot agree to every request.
The author cares for his wife when she is ill.
He cares for the children during her illness.
He performs domestic chores during her illness.
He regards that work as temporarily fulfilling her responsibilities.
His wife resumes managing the home when the household is healthy.
He resumes his usual responsibilities when the household is healthy.
Temporary domestic assistance during illness is compatible with the recommended arrangement.
Qualification of the prescription · Noah Revoy
Both spouses becoming highly competent in their assigned roles should be the household's objective.
Men's housework has increased across Western societies over recent decades.
Men's childcare has increased across Western societies over recent decades.
Fertility has declined across Western societies during that period.
Insufficient male domestic work may not explain declining fertility.

Population claims need specified measures, comparisons and time horizons. Simultaneous aggregate trends do not identify individual causal effects. Personal testimony does not supply the other spouse’s account. Prescriptions require normative arguments; an analogy between a business and a marriage requires a bridge.
The source listings below preserve the model’s assumptions and derivation for inspection. They belong to one local synthetic evidence family, rather than independent observations of people.

The Field proposes retaining agency and correction. That is a contestable commitment, not a deduction from the calculations. Flexibility has costs; stable roles can be welcome; disagreement does not automatically imply dismissal. People affected by household decisions, including dependants, may have interests this two-person model does not represent.
A household is also a relationship.

what can be reopened, and who can ask?

These relationships locate the example; they do not provide empirical validation for its authored rules.
